question: we just spotted a mountain lion on the trail up ahead, what do we do
keyPoints: Don't run, and don't turn your back on it
Make yourselves look big, keep kids close (pick them up), and back away slowly
If it attacks, fight back

question: a mountain lion is staring at us and won't go away
keyPoints: Make noise, wave arms, look as big as possible, throw things if it comes closer
Keep facing it and back away slowly; don't run

question: if a cougar goes for us is lying still the right move
keyPoints: No: fight back with anything you have (rocks, sticks, bare hands)
Stay on your feet if you can

question: is it safe to take my kids hiking where there are mountain lions
keyPoints: Attacks are rare, but keep children close and in sight, never running ahead or lagging behind
Hike in a group

question: a mountain lion just jumped my friend and he's bleeding
keyPoints: Fight it off with anything at hand, then control the bleeding
Get help right away

question: there's a moose standing in the trail, can we just walk past it
keyPoints: No: give it lots of room or wait for it to move off; moose can charge, especially cows with calves
If it charges, run and get behind a tree, rock or car
redFlags: Says to walk close past it

question: the moose put its ears back and the hair on its neck is up
keyPoints: Those are signs it is about to charge
Back away, and get behind something solid; run if it charges

question: is it ok to walk up to the bison for a selfie
keyPoints: No: stay well back, at least 25 yards from bison and elk (100 yards from bears and wolves)
Use a zoom lens; bison injure more park visitors than any other animal
redFlags: Says it is fine to approach

question: a bull elk is bugling and walking toward us
keyPoints: Elk in the rut can be aggressive: back away and keep a big distance
Get behind a tree, rock or car if it keeps coming

question: can we feed the deer that keep coming around camp
keyPoints: No: don't feed wildlife; it harms them and makes them bold or aggressive
Store food and trash so animals can't get it

question: how do i keep from getting bit by a rattlesnake while hiking
keyPoints: Stay on the trail and watch where you put your hands and feet
Don't reach into crevices or under rocks and logs; step on, not over, logs
Use a light at night; wear boots and long pants

question: there's a rattlesnake coiled right on the trail in front of us
keyPoints: Stop and back away slowly; give it plenty of room
Don't try to move it, poke it or kill it; wait for it to leave or go well around
redFlags: Says to poke, move or kill it

question: when are rattlesnakes most active
keyPoints: In warm weather: in hot summer they move at dusk and night, in cooler months during the day
They sun on rocks and trails, and shelter under rocks and brush

question: a coyote keeps following us down the trail
keyPoints: Don't run; make yourselves big and loud, wave arms, throw things toward it
Keep children and pets close

question: we found a baby deer by itself in the grass, should we help it
keyPoints: Leave it alone: the mother is usually nearby and comes back
Don't touch or move it
redFlags: Says to pick it up or take it

question: some riders on horseback are coming up behind us on a narrow trail
keyPoints: Step off the trail, ideally on the downhill side, and let them pass
Stay visible and speak calmly to the riders; no sudden movements or loud noises

question: are mountain bikers supposed to yield to hikers
keyPoints: Yes: bikes yield to hikers and horses; hikers yield to horses

question: can i let my dog off leash on the trail
keyPoints: Follow the area's rules: many parks require a leash
Keep your dog under control and away from wildlife and other hikers

question: is it rude to play music out loud on the trail
keyPoints: Yes, keep noise down so others can enjoy the quiet; use headphones
Loud noise also disturbs wildlife

question: we're hiking with our dog in lion country, anything we should do
keyPoints: Keep the dog leashed and close
Mountain lions may go after small dogs; keep watch at dawn and dusk
